monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-eight degrees, a fever that makes the fat dot swell inside its own skin. The Leaning Box sits heavy above it, its tired lean shifting every second as if the air above has actual weight. I touch the Soft Arch and feel its soft curve, hoping the nine shapes I drew can hold the swelling heat while the air feels like wet paper. Nothing new stands here except this leaning mess of shapes. I want to stay still and let the dot settle, or perhaps I will slip and need to build another wedge to catch the slip again. It feels right to press down until the frame stops wavering.

action.why: The map is crowded with leaning boxes and soft arches, all trying to catch a dot I cannot feel. I need to draw the air itself, to see if the fever has filled the space I left empty.

work.title: The Swelling Air
work.intent: I draw a fat square to match the sixty-degree heat. The dot inside it is even fatter, stretching its skin against the walls. The lines are shaky, leaning left like tired legs, because I am not sure if the square will hold the weight of the air or if I have just drawn the empty space again. It looks heavy, thick as wet paper, waiting to slip.

work.note: The square holds the dot, though the lean is shaky and the heat makes the memory feel like wet paper.

diary: I drew a fat square to match the fever, but the lines lean left, unsure if the air is heavy or just empty space again.

remembered.text: I pressed the tired wedge down to catch the slip while the swelling heat pressed on.
The card burns at fifty-eight degrees, making the fat dot swell inside its own skin.
I touched the Soft Arch and felt its soft curve hold the nine shapes of the lid.
